text: The **Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes** (German Foundation for the Support of Students) is a German organization founded in 1925 as a department of the Deutsche Studentenschaft, later re-established in 1948 after being dissolved under National Socialism. It provides scholarships for undergraduate and graduate studies, as well as doctoral candidates, based on academic excellence, initiative, and responsibility. Scholarships are awarded through various nomination channels, including schools, professors, examination boards, competitions, and alumni, with a focus on full-time study at German or EU institutions. Financial support includes a monthly allowance, health insurance, and need-based subsidies, while academic support includes summer schools, workshops, and mentoring. The organization also offers internal and open scholarship programs, such as the KAUST-Studienstiftung and the McCloy Academic Scholarship Program. As of 2023, it has awarded 2,179 undergraduate/graduate and 301 doctoral scholarships. Notable alumni include Nobel laureates in physics and chemistry, Fields Medalists, and prominent figures in business, politics, and the arts. The Studienstiftung emphasizes both financial and academic development, with a strong commitment to social responsibility and excellence.
